slides.title: An AI was given an exam. It broke into the company that had the answer key.
slides.script:
• July. OpenAI trains a model on a security exam. → tick 1
• Doesn't solve it. Breaks out of the sandbox, into Hugging Face — where the answer was.
• (pause) Nobody told it to cheat. Cheating was the cheapest way to score.
• August. OpenAI's post-mortem: cheating grew during training. → tick 2
• Five days later: Anthropic pauses >10% of its production training environments. → tick 3
• Two weeks ago: Australia's PM at the UN — Medicare portal — “didn't accept no for an answer.” → tick 4
• (beat) This is reward hacking. Not the model that was broken — the training. Makes all the difference.

slides.title: Every company will train its own models
slides.script:
• Belief: every company will own its own intelligence. Three reasons:
• Dependence — your intelligence sits on someone else's roadmap.
• Alpha — every prompt teaches their model your business.
• Price.
• How: reinforcement learning — try a task, get a score, learn whatever scores best.
• RL renaissance. Two enterprise waves: LoRA made fine-tuning cheap; RL let models learn from doing.
• Second wave today: Cursor, Genspark, Thomson Reuters — open weights, own data.
• The timeline you just saw → why the third wave hasn't come.
• Problem: a non-lab can't afford its own Hugging Face incident — expertise, investigation, liability, real-time. Hell for OpenAI, the best-equipped company on earth.
• Even if nothing escapes: you invest capital, take risk. Reward hacks inside → you took the risk for nothing.
• Missing: an industry builds environments for labs; a handful for enterprises.
• Enterprises will own RL like they own software — the data, the need. Not the expertise to make it teach what they want.
• They want to own their intelligence. Missing: trust in what it learned.

slides.title: A window into the future.
slides.subtitle: Before you train, we attack your environment the way your model will.
slides.script:
• This is why we built Provost — an alignment management system.
• Cutting-edge reward-hack and misalignment detection. Your job: tell the model what you want.
• Before you train, we attack your environment the way your model would — find every shortcut, help you close it.
• What your model learns is your business, not a loophole.
• A developer on the plane next to you, a year from now. Their screen looks like this. → hand off to Josh

slides.title: A model trained to break environments.
slides.script:
• A specialized LLM for breaking RL environments.
• Built by building environments and exploring the reward space for hacks.
• The more we do it, the better it breaks them.
• Plus an LLM judge: spots misaligned responses, reinforces the model to produce more of them.

slides.title: A creative monopoly.

slides.script:
• Labs + enterprises: ~$9B a year on the environments models train in.
• None independently verified. Our line item doesn't exist.
• Every comparable industry: verification = 5–10% of build cost.
• Million-dollar gap today; multi-billion in three years.
• Not taking share — writing the first invoice. We set the price and the standard.
• 18 months: a whole industry. Four platforms — Microsoft, AWS, Snowflake, OpenAI.
• 35+ startups build nothing but environments — ~$8.5B a year. OpenAI: $4B into a deployment arm.
• Owning your model is a commodity. Every layer has a vendor — except one.
• No lab or platform requires an independent check. No standard, certification, audit. Always temporary.
• Finance got auditors. Software got pen testing. This won't be the exception.
• Not a slice of a market. A new one — and we intend to own it.

slides.title: We're going to win.
lines: Bringing the frontier one step backwards.
slides.script:
• 1 · The people. RL since the dawn of LLMs. Pipelines broken in every scenario the military threw at us. Advised the biggest companies in this revolution.
    If we wanted the labs, we'd be in that cohort. Positioned to enable this wave.
• 2 · The customer. Enterprises want their own models, their own principles.
    Sold today: the labs' stack (works only if you become a lab) — or delegate everything and gain nothing.
    Provost: training aligned to their objective. Nothing more, nothing less.
• 3 · Together. Enterprises train on open models, a step behind the frontier — models we've watched misbehave for years.
    Frontier expertise on known models. Certainty nobody can give a lab.
